variables.name: Real GDP growth
variables.current: Reported fact: real GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY2026-27 under MoSPI's 2022-23-base series.
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: domestic activity should remain supportive, but the unusually strong first-quarter pace should not be extrapolated mechanically.
variables.earnings_impact: Supports revenue growth for domestically exposed lenders, consumer franchises and project suppliers; operating leverage depends on input costs.
variables.sector_market_impact: Positive for banks, NBFCs and capital goods; neutral-to-positive for discretionary demand, subject to affordability.
variables.source: MoSPI, Quarterly Estimates of GDP for Q1 FY2026-27

variables.name: Consumer inflation
variables.current: Reported fact: headline CPI inflation was 4.82% year-on-year in August 2026 (provisional); food inflation was 5.95%.
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: food-price volatility keeps the disinflation path uneven; September data were not yet released at the cutoff.
variables.earnings_impact: Higher food inflation can weaken real household purchasing power and complicate gross-margin recovery for consumer companies.
variables.sector_market_impact: Mixed for FMCG and discretionary; supportive of select pricing-power franchises but a risk to mass-market volumes.
variables.source: MoSPI, CPI Press Release for August 2026

variables.name: Monetary policy and rates
variables.current: Reported fact: the RBI kept the repo rate at 5.25% and retained a neutral stance at its August 2026 meeting.
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: future action is data-dependent; inflation persistence limits confidence in rapid easing.
variables.earnings_impact: Stable funding costs help planning, while transmission and deposit competition remain important for lender margins.
variables.sector_market_impact: Balanced for banks and NBFCs; rate-sensitive realty and autos benefit only if borrowing costs ease without a growth shock.
variables.source: Reserve Bank of India, MPC Resolution August 3-5 2026

variables.name: System liquidity
variables.current: Reported fact: RBI daily operations showed net liquidity absorption on September 30, 2026.
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: liquidity can change quickly with government balances, currency demand and RBI operations; one-day data are not a durable trend.
variables.earnings_impact: Adequate liquidity can reduce funding stress, though deposit pricing and asset-liability mix drive lender-level outcomes.
variables.sector_market_impact: Constructive for financial conditions; monitor for volatility rather than treating the observation as a directional call.
variables.source: Reserve Bank of India, Money Market Operations

variables.name: Fiscal impulse and public capex
variables.current: Reported fact: Union Budget FY2026-27 targets a 4.3% fiscal deficit and ₹12.22 lakh crore of capital expenditure.
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: execution quality and the crowding-in of private investment matter more than budgeted outlays alone.
variables.earnings_impact: Order inflows and utilization can support capital-goods earnings; fiscal consolidation helps macro stability.
variables.sector_market_impact: Positive for infrastructure, industrials, defence and power equipment; execution delays are the key transmission risk.
variables.source: Government of India, Union Budget 2026-27 FRBM Statement and Expenditure Budget

variables.name: Crude oil
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: treat oil as a two-sided external-balance and margin risk; no spot-price assumption is embedded.
variables.earnings_impact: Higher crude can pressure inflation, transport costs, working capital and margins for oil-consuming businesses.
variables.sector_market_impact: Negative sensitivity for OMCs, aviation, paints and logistics; upstream producers may benefit, subject to policy and realizations.
variables.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, petroleum market data (exact cutoff value not verified)

variables.name: INR and external conditions
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: global yields, oil and portfolio flows remain the main transmission channels; no FX target is assumed.
variables.earnings_impact: Currency weakness can aid exporter revenue translation but raises imported-input costs and foreign-currency liabilities.
variables.sector_market_impact: Mixed-positive for IT and pharma exporters; negative for import-intensive consumer, auto and energy users.
variables.source: Reserve Bank of India, Database on Indian Economy (exact cutoff value not verified)

variables.name: Global demand and risk appetite
variables.outlook_6_12m: Our analysis: slower external demand and volatile global discount rates argue for selectivity rather than a broad beta call.
variables.earnings_impact: Exporters face discretionary-spending and pricing risk; domestic earners have lower direct sensitivity.
variables.sector_market_impact: Cautious for IT and metals; supports a relative preference for domestic financials, healthcare and execution-led industrials.
variables.source: IMF World Economic Outlook and RBI Monetary Policy Report (no single verified cutoff figure used)

transmission_narrative: Our analysis: resilient domestic growth and public capex support demand and order books.
Reported inflation and a neutral RBI stance constrain the speed of monetary easing and keep funding-cost relief uncertain.
Food and imported-input volatility transmit into household purchasing power and corporate margins.
These channels favor balance-sheet strength, pricing power and execution visibility over indiscriminate cyclicality.
Valuation support requires earnings delivery; price weakness alone is not treated as evidence of undervaluation.
